clearer_why: B fits on one screen, puts Orders beside Payments with a visible charge arrow, and routes each edge to its own side of the target, with a legend explaining blue, dashed and coral. A stretches over two images, with Auth and Catalog arrows running 600px down to Redis and Orders stacked above Payments, so the reader has to trace long lines across the scroll.
looks_why: B has a coherent modern look: soft grey group panels, small type tags, bold names, and a restrained blue/coral palette. A has heavy black outlines, pastel pink/cyan/orange group fills, drop shadows and grey highlight boxes behind every edge label, which looks dated and cluttered.
weak_A: tall two-image sprawl with very long edges and boxy grey-highlighted labels
weak_B: small text and a few tight dashed routes (placed/settled) squeezed beside the Checkout core group

clearer_why: B lays out the agent, its model, memory, tools and storage in readable tiers with labels sitting on distinct edges and a legend. In A the Agent fans out four near-parallel vertical lines that run together, and the 'draw' and 'execute' labels collide on the lines, so it is hard to tell which line goes to which tool.
looks_why: B is balanced and polished, with icons, a subtitle, grey group panels and a highlighted Agent/Model API path in coral. A is tall and bare, with thick black arrows, saturated pastel group fills and grey label blocks, and a bundle of lines hanging below the Agent.
weak_A: bundle of parallel lines from Agent with overlapping draw/execute labels and a split across two images
weak_B: the svg and execute edges loop around and cross the Tools group, which is a little tangled

clearer_why: A shows the whole checkout platform in a single view, so the flow from clients to gateway to core to event bus to consumers is visible at once, with coral marking the checkout/charge path. Its weakness is that edges from Orders, Payments and Event bus share starting stems, which makes settled/card and placed/email slightly ambiguous. B routes every edge separately but is split over two images with very long lines to Redis.
looks_why: A uses rounded white cards, soft grey group panels and thin slate lines, which looks clean and current. B has heavy black outlines, shadows, pastel fills and grey label highlights, which looks like an older tool.
weak_A: shared edge stems (charge/write/placed and settled/card) and a meaningless 'box = step' legend, with node names crammed on one line
weak_B: tall two-image sprawl, very long Auth/Catalog lines, heavy dated styling

clearer_why: B keeps its labels on or next to their edges (prompt, search, events, persist, ingest) and sits at a manageable width with tools and storage laid out side by side. A sends five near-identical lines from the Agent down a very long right-hand gutter, with labels like 'prompt', 'search' and 'events' detached from their arrows and 'diagonaldi-agrams' hyphen-broken, so it is hard to tell which line goes where.
looks_why: A's rounded cards, muted palette and one orange highlight look more modern and calmer than B's heavy black borders, pastel fills and grey label blocks. Its comb of long parallel lines and large empty left side keep the advantage small, while B's draw/execute label collision is also unsightly.
weak_A: long parallel edge bundle with detached labels, a hyphen-broken node name and wasted empty space
weak_B: dated heavy styling, with parallel lines from the Agent and the draw/execute labels overlapping the lines
